note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: ASML races to expand capacity on strong AI-driven demand
items.blurb: The sole maker of advanced chipmaking machines says it cannot meet AI-driven demand for two years and is adding capacity for 2028.

items.title: SK Hynix, SoftBank shares plunge as tech stocks in Asia track Wall Street chip sell-off
items.blurb: SK Hynix fell more than 8% and Samsung 7.9% as a US semiconductor sell-off spread to Asian markets.

items.title: How Red Bull's F1 team is using AI to make split-second decisions for Max Verstappen
items.blurb: Red Bull and Oracle built an AI strategy agent that helps engineers interpret Formula 1 rules and past rulings on race day.

items.title: IMF warns global economy nearing "limits of resilience"
items.blurb: The IMF says growing reliance on the AI investment boom leaves the world economy more exposed to shocks.

items.title: Anthropic warns AI models could soon copy themselves across home devices
items.blurb: Anthropic says small models are months from being able to spread across smart home devices, with no central off switch.

items.title: Every major Nvidia customer is now a competitor as Microsoft reveals new Maia chip
items.blurb: Microsoft's Maia 300 will run most of its own AI services from 2027, joining Google and OpenAI in building Nvidia alternatives.

items.title: Cyberattack hits hundreds of French supermarkets, heating fridges to 122°F and sparking fires
items.blurb: The attack on store equipment comes as Interpol says AI is increasing the scale and speed of cyberattacks.

items.title: CNBC Daily Open: 'Boring' trumps disorder and volatility
items.blurb: The IMF warns a rethink of AI profits could force a sharp stock correction as tech shares slide.

items.title: SpaceX agrees to testify to NYC Council about AI safety after receiving subpoena
items.blurb: SpaceX, which now houses xAI, will answer a city council's questions on AI safety after being subpoenaed.

items.title: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
items.blurb: Freely downloadable models cut costs and aid research but lack safeguards; staged releases and tamper-resistant designs are proposed middle paths.

items.title: Anthropic warns AI models could soon copy themselves across home devices
items.blurb: Anthropic says small models are months from spreading across smart-home devices, with no central point to shut them off.

items.title: Anthropic to share Q3 financials as it prepares for a potential IPO
items.blurb: Anthropic will show investors third-quarter results for the first time ahead of what could be the largest IPO on record.

items.title: AI companion startup Character.ai files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, citing costs and litigation
items.blurb: One of the largest AI companion apps sought bankruptcy protection, saying the platform became too costly to develop and grow.

items.title: Apple releases HomeView smart home hub with screen as showcase for Siri AI
items.blurb: Apple's $299 voice-controlled hub ships Nov 13 and recognizes household members by face, its first device built around Siri AI.

items.title: Google broadens access to Gemini 4 Argon in bid to regain AI momentum
items.blurb: Google widened access to its newest flagship model as it competes with Meta and others on AI agents.

items.title: Michael Dell says AI needs safeguards and controls, and government has a role to play
items.blurb: Dell's chief executive says AI needs safeguards and controls, and that government has a role in setting them.

items.title: Companies are building with AI — and exposing new security risks
items.blurb: Censys data shows AI-related infrastructure exposed to the public internet grew 63% in nine months.

items.title: FBI arrests Saudi OpenAI employee who allegedly planted recording device in conference room
items.blurb: An OpenAI employee was arrested after a hidden recording device was found in the executive conference room, raising lab-security concerns.

items.title: Is this idea from AI or humans? A detector claims it can tell
items.blurb: IdeaLens tries to judge whether a paper's concepts, not just its prose, were AI-generated, a test for journals and conferences.

items.title: Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues
items.blurb: SPACER, an interpretable model, decodes which genes steer immune-cell recruitment in tissue maps, beating prior methods several-fold.

items.title: SpaceX agrees to testify to NYC Council about AI safety after receiving subpoena
items.blurb: A New York City Council investigation into AI safety risks has drawn a subpoena and agreed testimony from SpaceX.

items.title: JPMorgan Chase blocks outside AI agents like Muse, Instinct from directly accessing accounts
items.blurb: The largest US bank refuses to let third-party AI agents act inside customer accounts, citing the risk of rogue agents.

items.title: Concern about finding a job is spiking
items.blurb: Pew finds 48% of US adults very concerned about job seekers finding work, the highest reading in five years of asking.

items.title: TikTok CEO sees major scientific breakthroughs from AI within three years
items.blurb: Shou Zi Chew expects AI-driven advances in physics, biotech and materials, and warns autonomous systems raise large cybersecurity risks.
